region.name: SOC 2 Vendor Risk Compliance
region.summary: SOC 2 readiness and third-party risk work covering the Type I/II timeline, Q3 access reviews, vendor assessments for DriveWealth, Lithic, Plaid and AWS, concentration risks around Pillar Bank, and change-management controls such as feature flag approvals.

brief.text:
This region covers Stencil's SOC 2 program and third-party vendor risk management. Sam Whitfield runs the program and Maya Chen is the executive approver. Ledgerwise Assurance issued an unqualified SOC 2 Type I report on 2026-06-30, with controls tested as of 2026-05-31 against the Security and Availability criteria. The report had a clean opinion and 2 observations. The Type II observation window runs through the end of 2026, and fieldwork is scheduled for January 2027. Stencil decided not to ask Ledgerwise to shorten or restart the observation window. The status letter to Northfield will list the three known gaps plainly, without polishing them. One question is still open: whether the investing product, backed by the `brokerd` service, falls in Type II scope. Controls reported as healthy are change management (including feature flag approvals), offboarding, security training, backup restore testing and incident handling. Policy documents each have a named owner. The strategy doc is reviewed and revised every quarter so it does not go stale.

The Q3 access review covers 20 systems, tracked by tier, owner, account count, removals or reductions, and sign-off date. It ran late against its September 21-30 window. As of early October, 14 of the 20 systems (70%) were signed off. Plaid, Lithic, PagerDuty, Snowflake, Customer.io and Branch are still pending. An exception is to be documented, and the target completion date is 2026-10-10. The highest-severity open item is the policy that every vendor touching Confidential or Restricted data must be assessed before a contract is signed. A related todo requires every contract to include breach notification terms, data deletion on termination, and audit rights.

Vendor assessments set breach-notification SLAs against Stencil's 24-hour obligation to its sponsor bank, Pillar Bank. DriveWealth has strong controls overall, but its 72-hour breach notification window conflicts with that 24-hour obligation. Its sandbox also cannot simulate corporate actions, and its production credential access was cut from 3 engineers to 2. Lithic will receive Restricted and Confidential cardholder data and tokens at launch; its sandbox uses synthetic data only, and full card numbers never touch Stencil systems. Lithic's evidence includes a PCI DSS Level 1 AOC, a SOC 2 Type II report, a pen test summary, multi-region continuity with a 2-hour RTO, and a funding review. The Lithic findings are: pending Pillar Bank compliance approval (High, a launch blocker), no card fraud owner (Medium), and a 48-hour breach notification window (Low). Sandbox API keys had been shared too broadly; they were rotated and scoped to 3 people on 2026-10-01. The vendor risk register lists Tier 3 operational vendors such as GitHub, Persona (being phased out) and Sidekiq Pro, and flags concentration risk in Pillar Bank, Plaid and DriveWealth. Open contingency questions are whether to add a backup sponsor bank, whether to use MX as a Plaid backup, and what the alternative to DriveWealth would be. The register is reviewed quarterly and annually. Lower-severity open risks in this region are a fractional share position reconciliation fix and Android lagging iOS on investing screens. Typical questions about this region: Is Stencil SOC 2 compliant, and what is the Type II timeline? Which systems are holding up the access review? Which vendors fall short of the 24-hour breach notification requirement? What is blocking the Lithic card launch? Where is Stencil exposed to single-vendor concentration risk?

items.title: Decision: DriveWealth approved for continued production use
items.summary: Approved conditional on finding 1 being resolved or explicitly accepted by Maya by end of October.

items.title: Decision: Start Q4 access review Dec 1
items.summary: Q4 review will start Dec 1 rather than mid-December to avoid repeated lateness.
